summary: Within the package's frozen scope (listed legacy DMG imprisonment guidance captured 15 September 2026), the captured text does not support a single "custody only stops payment" rule across JSA, IS, SPC and ESA. DMG 12003 states the payability/entitlement distinction, but only for the benefits listed at 12002; DMG 12015 routes JSA and IS to Chapter 24, SPC to Chapter 78, ESA(Cont) to Chapter 53 and ESA(IR) to Chapter 54, each using a different mechanism. For legacy JSA(Cont) and JSA(IB) the captured text uses an entitlement condition (availability), with a limited 96-hour treatment at 24187. For IS (24212) and ESA(IR) (54213) the mechanism is a nil applicable amount, which the captured text links to loss of entitlement, with a remand branch (24214/54214) that may retain entitlement where there are allowable housing costs. For SPC the mechanism is nil credit rates and award revision (78666, 78672, 78675), with a remand exception. For ESA(Cont) the captured text shows suspension of payment from the first day (53257) and disqualification (53256), with days of disqualification exceeding six weeks not being days of entitlement (41823) while 41832 records other cases where entitlement continues though benefit is not payable. Package truncation: the assembly budget reports truncated = false with no omissions (52/64 nodes, 127/128 relationships, 487,506/524,288 bytes, depth 2), so no truncation is declared; however New Style JSA/ESA, UC and PIP ADM chapters and the Memo 07/20 body are outside the acquired evidence. This is an explanation of captured guidance, not a determination for any individual, and requires independent specialist review.

claims.statement: The captured general passage states that claimants are disqualified from receiving "these benefits" when imprisoned or detained in legal custody following criminal proceedings, that disqualification affects payability and not entitlement, and that payment can resume when the disqualifying conditions cease provided the conditions of entitlement remain satisfied, with no new claim normally needed on release unless entitlement was terminated.

claims.scope_or_qualification: The 12003 statement is expressly about "these benefits", i.e. the list introduced at 12002 (the captured page 2 list runs IB, MA, BPT, WMA, WP, WPA, BA, RP and continues 9.-17. SAP, GRB, AA, SDA, CA, DLA, IIDB, SP2, BSP). JSA, IS, SPC and ESA are not established by this passage; they are separately routed at 12015. Do not generalise 12003 into a rule that custody always leaves entitlement intact.

claims.statement: For Income Support, the captured mechanism is a nil applicable amount for a claimant who is a prisoner, and the captured note states that a claimant with an applicable amount of nil is not entitled to that benefit — so for IS the effect described is loss of entitlement, not merely non-payment.

The separate prisoner-in-hospital branch at 24215 can give either a nil applicable amount or full applicable amount depending on the admitting mental health legislation.

The captured chapter includes exceptions and branches that prevent a universal rule: no penalty imposed (53260), mentally disordered persons detained in legal custody (53268-53278), fine default (53267), detention abroad (53283) and suspension of payment for those not disqualified (53284, subject to 53285). New Style ESA is routed to ADM U6 and is not in the package.

gaps: ADM Chapters E3 (UC), P4 (PIP), S1 (new style JSA) and U6 (new style ESA) are named by 12016 but their bodies are not acquired, so custody effects for those benefits are not evidenced.

The body of DMG Memo 07/20, referenced in the frozen JSA, IS, ESA(IR) and ESA(Cont) prisoner headings, is absent; only a catalogue note recording its removal because the regulations ceased to have effect from 31 August 2021 is present.

No consolidated statutory text or case law is supplied; the footnote citations (e.g. SS CB Act 92 s 113(1)(b), IS (Gen) Regs Sch 7 para 8, SPC Regs reg 6/7, ESA Regs regs 159-161) are unreconciled references.
No evidence establishes which benefit regime, component or date applies to any particular claimant, and no personal facts are or should be supplied.
Chapter 53 exception detail for ESA(Cont) is partly present but the package flags unresolved internal references (53112, 53071) and the printed number 531261.
Partner, family-membership, hospital-legislation and housing-cost branches are only partially captured and would each need their own benefit-specific passage.
abstentions: Whether any individual claimant loses payment or entitlement to JSA, IS, SPC or ESA on imprisonment cannot be established from this package.
Whether the captured guidance reflects the law or guidance in force today (or at any date after the 15 September 2026 capture) cannot be established.
The effect of custody on New Style JSA, New Style ESA, Universal Credit or PIP cannot be stated, since the routed ADM chapters are outside the acquired evidence.
No amount, applicable amount, credit rate or award figure can be calculated or estimated from this package.
Whether the removed Memo 07/20 temporary treatment applies in any case cannot be established; its body is absent and it must not be revived.
Whether the generic 12003 payability statement can lawfully be applied to any benefit outside the 12002 list cannot be established here.
limitations: Independent experimental research, not an official DWP document, benefits advice, a calculation or an individual entitlement decision; all authored meanings and dependencies require specialist review.
"Sufficient" here means closure of the bundle-authored evidence requirements within the declared frozen scope, not a verified legal answer, current-law assurance or an individual decision.
The broad labels JSA and ESA do not establish a claimant's regime; regime and date must be confirmed and fresh authoritative checks made before applying any of this to a person.
The 12003 payability statement is scoped by the list at 12002 and cannot replace benefit-specific rules or show that entitlement always survives imprisonment.
Machine-extracted whole pages retain neighbouring text, footnotes, historical examples and possible reading-order errors; page presence is not full legal interpretation or PDF visual review.
Capture date is not publication, revision or commencement; amendment footers and example dates are literal source text.

Prisoner definitions differ by benefit; remand, bail hostel, sentence, release, hospital legislation, fine default, overseas detention, time limits and partner circumstances each require their own branch, and housing-cost passages do not establish a current housing award.
Source text, normalised extractions and the project's authored concept records carry different authority; none of this, nor this review, constitutes expert or specialist approval.
The assembly budget reports truncated = false with no omissions, but the package is nonetheless a bounded selection and absence of a conflict report does not prove absence of contradictions.
This is a model trial output requiring independent human review.
